@graph.headline: Proving What the AI Said Six Months Later
@graph.description: Your compliance framework already requires a record of what your AI system said, on which model version, with whose review — and vendors retire models on published schedules. Here are the four layers of proof, the seven fields a log has to hold, and a thirty-minute drill that shows whether you could answer a subpoena about an AI decision you made last spring.

about.name: Model provenance — the evidentiary record a business needs to prove what an AI system said, on which model version, under which policy, with whose review. Covers the four layers of proof (input, model identity, output, governing policy); the regulatory basis in 45 CFR §164.312(b) audit controls and §164.316(b)(2)(i) six-year retention; ABA Formal Opinion 512 (July 29, 2024) and Florida Bar Ethics Opinion 24-1 (January 19, 2024); vendor model retirement and OpenAI's 2026-10-23 shutdown cohort; the reproducibility limit documented by Thinking Machines Lab ('Defeating Nondeterminism in LLM Inference', September 10, 2025) where batch-variant kernels mean temperature zero is not deterministic and batch-invariant kernels restore it at roughly 20% throughput cost; discovery treatment of AI logs as ESI under Fed. R. Civ. P. 34, In re OpenAI (S.D.N.Y., preservation order May 13, 2025; 20 million logs ordered December 2, 2025) and Flagg v. City of Detroit, 252 F.R.D. 346 (E.D. Mich. 2008); the seven-field log schema; logging as a second copy of protected information; and why on-premises local LLM deployment with a hashed weights file provides a fixed referent for six-year obligations.

mainEntity.name: How long do we have to keep records of AI interactions?

acceptedAnswer.text: For HIPAA-covered work, six years. 45 CFR §164.316(b)(2)(i) requires retaining security documentation for six years from creation or from when it was last in effect, whichever is later. Litigation holds can extend that further, and a hold suspends routine deletion immediately.

mainEntity.name: Are AI chat logs discoverable in litigation?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. They are electronically stored information under Rule 34, and courts have treated data on third-party servers as within a party's control — Flagg v. City of Detroit, 252 F.R.D. 346 (E.D. Mich. 2008). In In re OpenAI (S.D.N.Y.), a May 2025 order compelled preservation of output logs over privacy objections.

mainEntity.name: Does setting temperature to zero make an AI's answers reproducible?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. Thinking Machines Lab showed in September 2025 that standard inference kernels are not batch-invariant, so server load alone changes the output. Batch-invariant kernels restore determinism at roughly a 20% throughput cost. Log the answer; do not plan to regenerate it.

The record of four things: what went in, which model version produced the output, what came out, and which policy governed the exchange. It is what lets a business answer "what did the system tell you" with a file instead of an estimate.

mainEntity.name: Can screenshots of the AI's answers satisfy this?

acceptedAnswer.text: Only as a last resort. A screenshot has no verifiable hash, no version string, and no reviewer identity, so it proves an image existed rather than what the system produced. A HIPAA-ready AI deployment captures the structured row at the moment of the request instead.
